fields.h1: Build a Shift Change Form That Confirms Coverage First
fields.hero_description: Build a shift change form that gets the covering coworker's yes, counts overtime and sends each request to the right manager.
fields.features_heading: What a Shift Change Needs Before Approval
fields.features_subheading: Six parts Emergent builds into the form, so a manager decides with the cover and the hours already known.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the request type

Pick swap and the form asks who is covering and which of their shifts you take in return. Pick drop and it asks for the shift, the reason and nothing at all about a trade.
fields.feature_2:
A yes from the coworker taking the shift

The covering coworker gets a link by email or Slack to accept or decline. Managers see a request only after that coworker accepts, so no approval rests on a guess about cover.
fields.feature_3:
Weekly hours added up before approval

The app adds the new shift to the hours each person already has scheduled that week. Any change that crosses the limit you set is marked in red and held for a manager.
fields.feature_4:
Each location's requests to its own manager

Requests from the downtown store go to its manager in Slack and the airport store's go to another by email. A request left undecided for 24 hours sends that manager a reminder.
fields.feature_5:
One row per change in a database you own

Every request saves who asked, who covered, who decided, and when. An approved change updates the schedule table and can sync to the scheduling tool you connect through its API.
fields.feature_6:
The full codebase, yours to move

On paid plans, export the code to your GitHub repository and host the form on servers next to your HR systems. Keep building on it in your own editor or with more prompts.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Employers Handle Shift Changes
fields.tab_content_1:
Hamish sees it only after Esteban agrees

Zofia Kral wants Saturday night off and offers her telemetry shift at Harlow Bay Medical Center to Esteban Molle. He accepts on his phone first. Only then does it go to Hamish, the charge nurse, with both nurses marked as telemetry trained. He approves, and the unit schedule shows Esteban on Saturday night.
fields.tab_content_2:
Picked up 14 minutes after it was posted

Nobody volunteers for the 6 a.m. Sunday opening at Brisk Bean. Tadeo can't make this one and drops it into the open pool. Every barista trained to open gets a Slack message, and Oksana claims the shift 14 minutes later. The store manager approves her pickup in Slack.
fields.tab_content_3:
Soraya decides any swap with overtime in it

Bartek has 40 hours at Bramblegate Distribution this week when he asks for a coworker's 6-hour Friday shift, which would make 46. Federal law gives covered employees overtime pay for hours worked over 40 in a workweek. That swap waits for Soraya, the shift lead, to decide.
fields.tab_content_4:
No one at Quayside changes more than Remy

Quayside Grocers keeps every shift change, approved or declined, in one table. Store manager Delvin sorts October's changes by employee. Remy leads with 6 changes against a store average of 2, every one a Saturday morning. Delvin takes Remy off Saturday mornings rather than approve the same swap each week.

fields.hero_prompt: Build a shift change form where staff can swap or drop a shift, the coworker covering it confirms, and the manager approves.

faq_plan.q: What is a shift change form?
How do I create a shift change form?

plan.angle: The top 10 is two public-employer PDFs (Boone County, DBHIDS), static template galleries (123FormBuilder, Jotform x2, pdfFiller, pdfRun, Workforce.com) and an Indeed letter guide. Every one is a blank form someone prints or fills in; none shows the employer what happens after the request: the coworker agreeing to cover, the check that the cover can work that shift, the overtime math and the manager's decision. This page is for the employer who schedules hourly staff: four shift change setups built from a prompt (a two-sided nurse swap, an open shift picked up from a pool, a swap that would cross 40 hours, a monthly change history), a how-to on what to ask and who approves, and an FAQ for the person who runs the schedule. It stays clear of recurring availability and time off, which have their own pages.
tab_stories: At Harlow Bay Medical Center, nurse Zofia Kral asks to give her Saturday night shift to Esteban Molle; Esteban confirms on his phone first, and only then does charge nurse Hamish see the request, with both nurses' telemetry sign-off shown.
A Brisk Bean barista, Tadeo, drops his Sunday 6 a.m. opening shift into the open pool; Oksana claims it 14 minutes later and the store manager approves the pickup from Slack.

At Bramblegate Distribution, picker Bartek asks to take a Friday shift that would bring his week to 46 hours; the form counts his hours, marks 6 of them as overtime, and holds the swap for shift lead Soraya.

Quayside Grocers keeps every approved and declined change in one table; in October, Remy has 6 changes against a store average of 2, and manager Delvin sees him at the top of the list before the next schedule goes out.
